correctness.rationale: A face of a join of three one-dimensional factors has at most 2 vertices per factor; D³ is a graph. Every 3-face has occupancy (1,1,1) or permutation (2,1,0). A pair of 3-faces forms a six-face only when occupancy patterns sum to (2,2,2), giving exactly the four disjoint categorical graph products, with no missing or cross-type edges. Synchronized walks in connected graphs have eventually all feasible lengths of the correct parity; bipartite factors impose only relative color parity. Thus G1×G2×G3 has 2^(b−1) components when b>=1 (one if b=0), while Gi×K_(e_j,e_k) has two if Gi is bipartite else one. Direct edge counts 4e1e2e3 and 2e1e2e3 per block and explicit color-class vertex counts determine E−V+1 per connected graph. Independently enumerated all 3-face complementary pairs for three equal-face-vector witnesses, yielding common (V,E)=(252,1080) and componentwise ranks (82,82,82,82,163,163,181); (82,82,163,181,325); (163,163,181,325), agreeing with parity counts 7,5,4. Each original factor C6 and C5 plus leaf has 6 vertices/6 edges and |.|~S¹, so all joins share the same face vector and S⁵ homotopy. All conclusions use graph proof, not finite extrapolation.
residual_risks: Tuples of complexes with filled 2-simplices or disconnected factor graphs fall outside hypotheses.
The three explicit witnesses verify the distinguishing boundary, while arbitrary factors rely on synchronized-walk parity proof.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge with transparent partial coverage. A published exact classification for THREE POLYGON BOUNDARIES gives the same four-product splitting and parity formula in the special case Gi=C_m, where all bipartition shores are equal. The assigned theorem genuinely extends to arbitrary connected graph complexes including leaves and unequal shores, and adds three same-f-vector sphere-homotopy counterexamples not implied by the polygon theorem. Weichsel supplies the classical graph direct-product connectedness fact, explicitly treated as prior, not new. Lesh–Schreiner–Wahl gives only qualitative weak-Cohen–Macaulay connectivity bounds.
residual_risks: An unindexed arbitrary-graph extension of the polygon result may exist; checked relevant results do not cover it.
Witness complexes with pendant edges are homotopy spheres but not necessarily manifold triangulations; that limitation is explicit.
